# Election update: Thursday, November 12 (morning)

## Bottom line
The House results table marks 426 races called: D 257, R 169, with 218 needed for a majority ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). This morning's parse missed Delaware's at-large row, which the table marked called for Rep. Sarah McBride (D) on Wednesday, so the Democratic count is one seat low. In the Senate, Scott Colom (D) won Mississippi, the New York Times reports ([NYT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxPRTNHZFFRdHFUWjJ5Yk4xZGNtemYyR3B3UENkcHE3NG5TOUo3ai0ydnFGQ2k5YU1IbkNLdG4tNHR4dTZES01xQVlrMHN2YUdVUVJoQzNEcFdzN3N2Q1d0Z0lwZE1sM2I0dGFZY250Zk91QUtjczEtS1dsQTh0YjJ5MmpxZkltaGU0R2J3MXpqSzMxdw?oc=5)). That brings Democrats to 55 seats and Republicans to 44, counting seats not up, with Alaska the last uncalled race ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Governors: D 28, R 20 of 50, counting the 14 states with no race this year; Alaska and Kansas are not called, and five seats flipped, all to Democrats ([governor table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections)). Three seats rated Solid R came in within 5 points; Republicans held all three.

## Called since the last update
- **Flips (2, both D):** SEN-MS, where Colom unseated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R) and became Mississippi's first Black senator in about 150 years, the BBC reports ([BBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE9GTWpzUWs1VjNiQ09nTDg5VjZ2eFh4aGxITHRBWmtybXRCekpoRHNkbkpuNGhoTng1NG1LV0U3Sm1sb0xBY0J3WjQzVVJweTd0UVB6VWxkX0pZMW8?oc=5)); HOU-NC-03, where Rep. Greg Murphy (R) conceded to Democrat Raymond Smith Jr. ([The Hill](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Hold (1, R):** HOU-SC-02 **(rated safe)**: Rep. Joe Wilson (R) won reelection after a recount confirmed a narrow victory, about 1 point in the table ([WLTX](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Rated safe, came in close:** OK-05 (Rep. Stephanie Bice, R, by 1.3 points) and OK-01 (Rep. Mark Tedford, R, by 4.6 points), both called for the Republicans in the table ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- No governor race was called.

## Recounts and certification
- **South Carolina:** recounts confirmed the ouster of a legislative majority leader and a narrow Greenville County Republican win, the South Carolina Daily Gazette reports ([SC Daily Gazette](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **North Carolina:** NC-07 is within recount range, per the Charlotte Observer ([Charlotte Observer](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Kansas:** the state certifies Nov. 16; recount requests are due by 5 p.m. Nov. 17 ([KWCH](https://www.kwch.com/2026/11/10/nearly-week-after-midterm-election-governors-race-is-still-too-close-call/)).

## Coverage note
- **Parser:** the Senate (35) and governor (36) tables parsed fully and the parser check is healthy. The House table parsed 434 of 435 rows; Delaware's at-large row was missed, so the House Democratic count is one low. The parser fix is left for an attended session.
- **Court records:** CourtListener used (4 requests; 36 election dockets and 2 opinions).
- **Scorecard:** 95.2% of competitive races called; Lessons learned returns weekly (next around Nov. 16).
